why_this_block_exists: It explains the fields below without relying on JSON comments, which are not valid JSON.
prompt_authoring: Prompts may be string, string array, or prompt_file.
This shipped workflow keeps the prompt inline as an array; the long reusable policy
lives in `globals.triage_rules` as a file include.
globals: `globals.triage_rules` is an include descriptor for the shared triage template.
The step pulls it in with `include: ["{{globals.triage_rules}}"]`.
This avoids duplicating the template text inside the operational prompt.
defaults: Defaults make omitted step fields slow/coding with read/source/type/grep/git/callers+edit actions.
The triage step repeats those fields explicitly and emits both the human summary
and the structured triage_coding object in one response.
ordering_parallelism_failure: The eval requires `summary_written == true`; a verdict without summary.md
is retried rather than reported as success.
Driver, edit, repeated missing-summary errors, or missing triage_coding JSON fail

title: Triage a kres finding into summary.md
description: Read a kres finding directory (FINDING.md + metadata.yaml), classify the status, write summary.md, sync metadata.yaml + FINDING.md status, and emit structured triage_coding JSON.

target.description: Absolute path to a kres finding directory (the kres --export shape — must contain FINDING.md and metadata.yaml).

steps.title: Classify the finding and emit summary.md
prompt: {{workflow.target}}
Triage the kres finding at the absolute path above. Apply the rules in the embedded
triage template (see INCLUDES). Emit `summary.md` and synchronized severity updates
to `metadata.yaml` + `FINDING.md` as `code_output` entries with absolute paths under
that directory. Also update status/subsystem in those files when the template requires it.
Return a `verdict` field in your structured outputs naming the chosen status (one of:
Fixed | Plausible | Unconfirmed | Unknown | Invalid | NotADefect | ConfirmedLatent). The machine
`triage_coding.summary_status` is the lowercased verdict for the single-word
statuses; the exceptions are `ConfirmedLatent` -> `confirmed_latent` and `NotADefect` -> `not_a_defect`.
Return a `severity` field in your structured outputs naming the chosen severity
(one of: high | medium | low).
Also return `triage_coding` as a structured object derived from the same summary.md
content you emit. Do not put this JSON inside summary.md. Shape:
- schema_version: integer, set to 1
- severity: one of high, medium, low
- summary_status: one of fixed, plausible, unconfirmed, unknown, invalid, confirmed_latent, not_a_defect
- summary_subject: short subject string from the summary, or empty string
- impact_classes: array of lowercase strings such as local_dos, remote_dos, memory_corruption, privilege_escalation, info_leak, data_corruption, vm_escape, latent, test_only, unknown
- config_commonness: one of common, niche, debug_or_test_only, unknown

- reject_reasons: array of lowercase strings for reasons this should not enter a fix queue, such as invalid, unconfirmed, unknown_reachability, latent_only, intentional_design, test_only, niche_config, fixed_already

- reachability: object with host_access, remote_access, root_required, regular_user as yes/no/n/a/unknown strings, plus build_config {required, symbols[]} for compile-time gating and runtime_state {required, conditions[]} for everything that must additionally hold at run time. Keep those two apart: CONFIG_X=y and X_enabled() are different conditions.
- touches: object with files array and subsystems array, populated only from explicit summary text
- actionability: object with fix_queue_eligible boolean and rationale string
- priority: object with tier one of critical, high, medium, low, none, unknown; score integer 0-100; reason string
- evidence: object with status, impact, reachability, and actionability strings quoting or summarizing the summary text that supports the classification

verdict.description: Status the agent assigned to the finding.

severity.description: Severity assigned by triage and written to metadata.yaml, FINDING.md, and summary.md.

summary_written.description: Machine-populated. True only when this step emitted and wrote a non-empty summary.md.

severity_written.description: Machine-populated. True only when this step emitted summary.md, metadata.yaml, and FINDING.md and their persisted contents contain the chosen severity.

followups.description: Typed requests for missing source/type/history/context if the finding cannot be triaged from the supplied files alone.

code_output.description: Files emitted by the triage step, normally absolute DIR/summary.md and optional metadata/FINDING status updates.

symbols.description: Kconfig symbols that must be set, e.g. CONFIG_SCHED_CORE=y.

conditions.description: Static branches, sysctls, scheduler features, cgroup settings, topology — conditions that must hold at run time even when the build config is set.

runtime_state.description: Runtime gating. Distinct from build_config: a kernel can have CONFIG_X=y while X_enabled() is false.

triage_coding.description: Structured classification derived from the generated summary.md content.

eval.expr: summary_written == true && severity_written == true && triage_coding.schema_version == 1 && triage_coding.severity == severity
